pageCache.text:
Welcome to Hamilton Lodge School and College.
I am proud to introduce Hamilton Lodge School and College, a well-respected specialist school and residential provision offering aspirational, and highly personalised education and care for deaf children and young people, including those with additional Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).
At Hamilton Lodge, we believe that knowing every learner well is at the heart of great education. We take the time to understand each child and young person — their strengths, aspirations, interests, needs, and experiences — so that they feel welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to participate fully, achieve highly, and thrive during their time with us, and throughout their future lives.
Our highly skilled school and residential teams have expertise in supporting learners who may lack confidence, have experienced barriers to learning or require additional support to realise their potential. We combine high-quality education with exceptional residential care, helping our learners to develop not only academically, but also as confident, resilient, and increasingly independent young people. We place a strong emphasis on communication, life skills, employability, and preparation for adulthood, ensuring that our learners are equipped with the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to succeed in employment, further education, and independent living.
Our whole-school community shares a deep commitment to our learner's success. The staff, leaders, and governors maintain high expectations and believe passionately in what every child and young person can achieve. This ambition and impact were recognised in our positive school inspection report in 2025 and our most recent residential inspection in February 2026. The residential inspection highlighted that our provision “provides highly effective services that consistently exceed the standards of good”, with the actions of the school contributing to “significantly improved outcomes and positive experiences for children and young people.”
We are registered to educate and care for learners ages 5 to 19 and are committed to continuous improvement. We achieve this by continuing to evolve our curriculum, strengthening our specialist provision, and developing purposeful partnerships with local schools, colleges, and other organisations.
We want our learners to leave Hamilton Lodge with a strong sense of identity and belonging, the confidence to advocate for themselves, and the skills and independence to take their place in society and shape their own future.
We are ambitious for every learner. We believe in their potential, celebrate their individuality, and are committed to ensuring that deafness and additional needs never limit what they can achieve. We look forward to welcoming you and your family to Hamilton Lodge School and College.
Kirstie Fulthorpe Interim Headteacher

Careers programme.
kirsty.mcginn@hamiltonlsc.co.uk
Independent Careers advisor
careers@hamiltonlsc.co.uk
Summary of programme
We provide independent careers advice for all learners from year 9 onwards with our independent careers adviser, Carl Jackson.
Kate works alongside school and FE staff to provide a range of activities to raise awareness of options for our learners and they work together to encourage learners to join in external careers fairs such as at the Amex stadium and at our partner colleges.
It is our aim that every learner, for whom it is deemed appropriate, should have first hand experiences of the workplace through visits, a placement or experiences in school. Workplace experiences are delivered within the school setting especially when students are unable to access settings outside of school.
Any employers or anyone who would be interested in getting involved or offering placements for our learners, please contact careers@hamiltonlsc.co.uk
More Information for parents/carers/learners
More information on careers and work for young Deaf learners can be found on the NDCS website.
Assessing the impact of our programme.
We evaluate our programme against the 8 benchmarks used by the Compass Careers Benchmark tool.
This guides our development plan for careers and provides us with a rationale for focussed support.
You can see more information about our work based learning and careers programme here:
Programme and Provider Access at our school
Programme and Provider Access will be reviewed in the summer of 2025.
We welcome feedback on our careers programme from learners, parents/carers and employers. Please email any comments or suggestions to:

Additional Grants:
Pupil Premium:
The Pupil Premium is additional funding given to schools so that they can support particular groups of pupils who are known to be at risk of underachievement and close the attainment gap between them and their peers. The Pupil Premium is allocated to schools for pupils, in Years R to 11, who are known to be eligible for free school meals (FSM) or who have been eligible for FSM in the past six years (Ever 6). Pupil Premium is also allocated for children who have been looked after by the local authority.
More information about the Pupil Premium is available on the Department for Education website.
How we use the pupil premium
Our allocation now comes from the ESFA.

Provision is reviewed regularly via scheduled meetings of our Pupil Support team of therapeutic staff.
We anticipate that as a consequence of these strategies and interventions, pupils for whom the Pupil Premium applies will make at least planned progress commensurate with their abilities.

More information for parents and carers
There are a range of ways that parents/carers can support their child with online safety. Here are some simple steps to help keep them safe online;
Open Discussion
Begin a discussion around how the internet will be used in your house. As a family discuss what information should be kept private (such as personal information, photos etc) and agree rules created by both parties for making and meeting online friends. Talk to your child about what they are doing online much like you would about their offline activities. Ask them to show you how they use the internet, learn which websites or tools they like to use and why. Learning together with your child can often open opportunities to discuss safe behaviour online. It’s essential to be realistic: banning the internet or websites you do not think are suitable often will not work and it can make a child feel less able to report a problem or concern, so education around safe use is essential.
Encourage sensible use of social sites
Social sites are rapidly becoming a significant part of young people’s lives and is how they often communicate with the world. Make sure your child is aware of risks and knows how to block and report people on their Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat or other social media sites if they receive nasty or inappropriate messages or content. Encourage your child not to retaliate or reply and to keep any evidence.
Location
Consider locating your computers and laptops in a family area where you can monitor your children’s online activity. Think about where you allow your child to use social media and video apps like Facetime, What’s App and SKYPE. Remember there are lots of devices which can be used to go online.
Follow the link for more guidance around safety information for consoles and devices.
Passwords
Passwords are key for keeping your child’s information safe. Discuss using strong passwords with your child so they understand how they can protect their online accounts. It’s important they know they need to keep their passwords safe and not share them with anyone or use the same password for several accounts. If your child’s account is “hacked” or compromised then make sure they change their password and report any concerns or suspicious activity.
Follow this link for more advice on using strong passwords. You can also check check how secure your passwords are by visiting security.org
Software
Make sure your antivirus software is up to date and your WIFI connection secure. Use Parental Control software for computers, laptops, mobile phones and games consoles to block unsuitable content or contact. Always remember that parental control tools are not always completely effective and sometimes unsuitable content can get past them, so don’t rely on them alone to protect your child. If this is something that you are unsure about doing, you can contact your internet provider who will support with these changes over the phone.

Curriculum Overview.
Communication & Learning
Language and communication are paramount in the development and learning for Deaf children. We want all our learners to develop their language skills and to be confident communicators. We focus on developing independence and nurturing our learners into developing a positive Deaf identity, self confidence and self esteem.
Our Curriculum offer
Our curriculum has been developed to best prepare our learners for life beyond our school and college. Our destination data helps inform our curriculum development, we review our curriculum offer annually to ensure it is fit for purpose and offers our learners the best possible opportunities to progress in their learning and follow their dreams.
We offer a range of accredited qualifications including Signature BSL, GCSE, Entry Level awards, Functional Skills and AQA Unit Awards. They are carefully matched to learners' ability, ultimately ensuring a curriculum offer that offers the right balance of access and challenge required to secure progress in their learning.
For our children who are not yet ready to access the full range of subject based learning or who have difficulty with transitions we have a Specialist Provision which is designed to meet their needs.
As an integral part of our offer we have a specially developed independent living programme to support our learners as they develop toward their adulthood.
